message: Can you look at this ECG? I think it might be a STEMI, right?
reply:
**I don’t see clear diagnostic ST elevation on this image, so I wouldn’t confidently call it a STEMI. But this ECG cannot rule out a heart attack.**

My read:
- Regular sinus rhythm, approximately **90 beats/minute**, with narrow QRS complexes.
- Some prominent chest-lead voltages and mild ST–T changes, but no convincing pattern of ST elevation in neighboring leads with reciprocal depression.
- Baseline drift and artifact make subtle changes harder to assess.

STEMI assessment depends on ST changes, symptoms, and comparison with previous ECGs. Ongoing symptoms may require repeat ECGs and troponin testing even when the initial ECG is nondiagnostic. [ACC/AHA guidance](https://www.jacc.org/doi/10.1016/j.jacc.2024.11.009)

**If there is chest pain, breathlessness, sweating, faintness, or new upper-body discomfort now, call emergency services and don’t drive yourself.** If already in a clinic or hospital, have the treating clinician review this immediately.

What symptoms prompted this ECG, when did they start, and what is the patient’s age?
